ca_black_flower.blurb: Black Flower is a broad, steep wall high on the Santa Monica ridgeline, between Calabasas and Malibu. It is almost entirely bolted face climbing, with a couple of trad lines mixed in. The lines follow thin edges, small pockets and seams, and most sit within a few degrees of vertical, so expect technical, fingery movement rather than big holds. Grades start in the 5.6 to 5.8 range but the bulk of the wall is 5.11 and 5.12, so it suits strong intermediates and up more than beginners. The wall sits only a short stroll from the road, and the early morning and evening hours find it in shade.

_expect.name: Soul Power Wall (rename approved by LCO)

ca_soul_power_wall_rename_approved_by_lc.blurb: Soul Power Wall is the first crag you meet when heading into the Central Gorge of the Owens River Gorge near Bishop, sitting at the foot of the trail from the rim. It is a single-pitch sport wall with roughly 100 feet of climbing, and nearly everything is bolted. Most routes fall between the 5.9 and 5.12 range, with the largest cluster at 5.10 and a solid group at 5.12, plus one 5.13. Mornings are cool and shaded and the stone warms up later in the day. The Central Gorge as a whole is the busiest part of the canyon, so expect company on good days.
ca_soul_power_wall_rename_approved_by_lc.parking_note: Use the Central Gorge parking area along Gorge Road, on the dirt beside the pavement. The trail down into the canyon begins right at that lot.
ca_soul_power_wall_rename_approved_by_lc.approach: From the lot, drop down a steep, loose class 2-3 gully to the dirt road in the canyon bottom. The wall is just above the restrooms at the base of the trail. Watch for rock falling onto the crag below.

ca_elephant_rock_3.blurb: Elephant Rock stands in the Lower Merced River Canyon, downstream of Yosemite Valley. It is mostly a crack-climbing venue, where splitters and hand cracks on the lower walls give way to a few steep bolted lines higher up on the upper wall. Grades run from 5.9 up through the 5.12s, with the greatest number in the 5.10 range, so it appeals to climbers comfortable on granite trad at the moderate-to-hard level. The cliff is described as a shady option that is quieter than the headline walls of the Valley proper. Getting to the base takes more effort than at a roadside crag.

ca_parking_lot_rock_3.blurb: Parking Lot Rock is a single, well-liked sandstone boulder in the Castle Rock area of the Santa Cruz Mountains, among the first boulders you reach on the way up the hill. It offers a varied set of problems on cracks, roofs, flakes and an arete, along with a traverse. Difficulty is wide: a handful of easy problems and then a solid middle at around V3 to V4, rising to a few V6 and V7 lines and some very hard sit-start projects up to V12. The sandstone here is fragile, so the boulder needs dry conditions.

ca_rimview_cliffs.blurb: Rimview Cliffs is a small sport area on the rim of the Sherwin Plateau, close to Mammoth Lakes in the Eastern Sierra, with views east over the Owens Gorge. The routes are short single-pitch lines on bolted welded tuff, around 50 to 60 feet, and no trad gear is needed. Grades are friendly: mostly 5.8 and 5.9 with a good block at 5.10, a couple of easier 5.6 and 5.7 routes, and only one 5.11. A beginner-oriented section has three easy lines that can be led or top-roped. Bring a helmet, as some rock is loose, and expect the east-facing wall to catch morning sun.
ca_rimview_cliffs.parking_note: Follow the road toward the Alcove but pull over roughly 100 yards before reaching it; the roadside pullout there is closest to the descent notch.
ca_rimview_cliffs.approach: A short scramble through a notch below the road drops you to the base, about five minutes from the car. Footing is a little steep, so move carefully.

ca_summit_rock.blurb: Summit Rock sits along Skyline Boulevard in the Santa Cruz Mountains near Castle Rock, and holds perhaps the greatest concentration of routes on any of the Skyline rocks. The climbing is a blend of bolted face routes, trad lines, top-rope setups and a few boulder problems, in a wide mix of rock character including chimneys, clean cracks and steep arete features. Grades range from about 5.7 to 5.12 on the rope, with the largest group in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. Many routes are easy to set up as top-ropes. It tends to be quieter than the main Castle Rock formation and has wide views over the Bay.
